definition: In this context, religion refers to a system of belief and motivation linked to prosocial behaviour and cooperation in large-scale societies. The source describes religiosity as tending to persist when external threats are common and important, and to decline when those threats lessen and anxiety falls.

reasons: The packet supports religion being associated with prosocial behaviour/cooperation and with changes in religiosity under external threats, but it does not support defining religion itself as a “system of belief and motivation.”
The statement generalizes the source’s specific model about a religiously motivated prosocial equilibrium into a broader definitional claim about religion without sufficient support.

The packet does not support the phrase “system of belief and motivation.” It only refers to “religiously-motivated prosocial equilibrium,” “religion,” and “religiosity,” without defining religion as a belief-and-motivation system.

The definition presents the external-threat/anxiety relationship as a general descriptive “tendency” (“tending to persist/decline”), but the packet is from an agent-based model and does not justify characterizing these as real-world tendencies.

The definition frames the account as general (“linked to prosocial behaviour and cooperation in large-scale societies”) without clearly tying it to the model’s conditions (“so long as external threats…” / “Once external threats are eliminated”).
